title: Spare GPU Pools & Failover Matrix — Q1 2026
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet evaluates current spare GPU pool placements and proposes an operational failover matrix for multi-region DR. Primary goal: ensure Redwood-hosted inference keeps within latency and throughput SLOs during regional outages while minimizing committed idle spend. Secondary: produce an actionable reserve schedule for Q2–Q4 2026.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Target warm spare: 8–12% of steady-state serving capacity per global fleet, distributed across region pairs rather than concentrated in a single cold pool.
- Hot-failover (automated routing) will be supported by cross-region prefix cache invalidation windows and pre-warmed model shards. Prioritized for enterprise Dedicated tenants and high-QPS routes.
- Cold-reserve (buffer we can spin up in 1–3 hours) maintained in two regions per hemisphere: primary/secondary pairing.
- Recommended initial reserve in Q2 2026: 120 H100-equivalent GPUs globally (approx mix H100: 70, A100-80GB: 40, L40s for embeddings: 10), distributed by failover matrix below.

Assumptions used in sizing:
- Baseline steady-state serving: 1,100 effective H100-equivalent GPUs (weighted by workload token-rate and model size).
- Acceptable RTO (automated routing + warm failover): <= 90 seconds for top-tier routes, manual escalation to 15 minutes for remaining customers via Dedicated burst capacity.
- Acceptable RPO: 0–60s for chat streaming (best-effort), 0 for idempotent text generation where client-level retries are fine.
- Typical regional capacity utilization target: 70–85% during peak; spare sits outside that target.

Failover matrix (primary -> preferred failover, warm/cold tier):
- us-west1 -> us-west2 (hot), us-east1 (cold)
- us-east1 -> us-west2 (hot), eu-west1 (cold)
- us-west2 -> us-east1 (hot), us-central1 (cold)
- eu-west1 -> eu-central1 (hot), us-east1 (cold)
- asia-east1 -> asia-southeast1 (hot), eu-west1 (cold)

Notes on pairing rationale: low network RTT between hot pairs, legal/data residency constraints considered for cold fallbacks (avoid moving regulated EU traffic to non-EU cold region without consent).

Proposed spare pool distribution (Q2 target by region, H100-equivalent):
- us-west1: spare hot 18 (reserve tier: 6 cold)
- us-west2: spare hot 20 (reserve tier: 8 cold)
- us-east1: spare hot 22 (reserve tier: 12 cold)
- us-central1: spare hot 10 (reserve tier: 4 cold)
- eu-west1: spare hot 18 (reserve tier: 10 cold)
- eu-central1: spare hot 12 (reserve tier: 6 cold)
- asia-east1: spare hot 12 (reserve tier: 6 cold)
- asia-southeast1: spare hot 8 (reserve tier: 2 cold)
Total hot spare: 120 H100-equiv (matches target).

Operational behaviors and automation triggers:
- Health-triggered routing: if primary region CPU/GPU == 95% or network packet loss >3% for 30s, mark region degraded and begin hot failover for prioritized routes.
- Auto-scale of warm pool: warm nodes keep 50% of model KV cache persisted and run a synthetic warmup trace every 10m to keep cold-start penalties <300ms.
- Prefix-level caching: cache keys tagged with region and prefix; on failover, invalidate prefix TTLs to avoid stale responses.
- Billing and cost control: warm spares run on spot preemptible with immediate fallback to on-demand when spot eviction rate >2% for >5m.

Model residency & pre-warm strategy:
- Maintain model shards for top-20 enterprise models fully resident across hot pair regions. For tail models, maintain small-weighted shards and rely on cold-reserve spinup.
- Quantization/variant strategy: pre-warm lowest-latency quantized profile used in production to reduce memory overhead. Full-precision shards stored on SSD-backed object storage for 1–3h spin-up.

Simulations & recent incident learnings (notes):
- Simulation on 2026-01-28 (regional outage window) showed: with 100-hot spare evenly distributed, p50 latency increase 18%, p95 35% unless KV caches were warmed; after warming, p95 delta improved by ~12pp.
- Incident IN-2025-11-02 indicated a single-concentrated spare pool in us-central1 caused long tail failover time due to network egress throttling and model fetch hot-spot. Hence decentralize spares.

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Cross-region bandwidth bottlenecks during mass failover. Mitigation: throttle warm fetches, serve degraded-latency plan with shorter context sizes. Owner: Marco Alvarez.
- Risk: Regulatory non-compliance for cold failover to non-compliant region. Mitigation: route regulated customers to pre-approved cold pools; tie to customer metadata. Owner: Leah Chen.
- Risk: Spot market instability leads to unavailable warm nodes. Mitigation: hybrid warm pool (70% spot, 30% on-demand). Owner: Omar Haddad.

Action items (next 8 weeks):
1) Implement routing policy flags per customer tier (priority, allowed fallback regions) — owner: Leah — due: 2026-02-14.
2) Run 3 chaos-drills focused on cross-region failover (one per hemisphere) — owner: SRE lead (Sofia) — start: 2026-02-01, complete: 2026-03-15.
3) Add metric dashboards: per-prefix failover latency, cache warmness score, and warm-pool eviction rate — owner: Observability team (Marco) — due: 2026-02-28.
4) Reserve procurement plan for Q2: negotiate 6–12 month reserved instances for core Dedicated enterprise customers to reduce wasted spend during idle reserve time — owner: Finance & Infra ops — due: 2026-03-01.

Open questions (to resolve before Q2 purchase commit):
- Exact model mix hedging: how many L40 vs H100 equivalents should be reserved for embeddings-heavy workloads? Proposal: reserve 10 L40 equivalents and re-balance quarterly.
- Tenant-level opt-in for cross-region cold failover (legal/contract addendum needed?).
- SLA language for warm-failover latency (do we commit to p95 <= X for failover windows?).

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call during regional outage
- Step 1: Confirm region health signals and determine primary/secondary status (SRE runbook ID: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENT-RUNBOOK-234)
- Step 2: Route enterprise-priority prefixes to hot pair region via routing policy API (automation should do this automatically if thresholds met)
- Step 3: Monitor cache-warmness and synthetic-warmup completion; escalate if >5m without warmup hits
- Step 4: If warm pool exhaustion predicted (forecast >90% of hot spare), enable cold spin-up playbook and notify customers in last-resort channel

This document is a working proposal and intentionally conservative on RTO/RPO assumptions. Feedback welcome — annotate this doc or add rows to the spreadsheet snapshot below with alternative numbers for sensitivity runs.
